subject: Discovery recap + procurement framing for Finarc analytics evaluation
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Megan Liu <megan.liu@finarc.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 15:03:00 -0500
Subject: Discovery recap + procurement framing for Finarc analytics evaluation

Hi Megan — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned. I’ve kept this intentionally short; happy to expand any section.

Key pain points you shared
- Intermittent latency spikes during end-of-day batch scoring (affects customer SLAs).
- Rising per-request cost from current MLOps setup; want predictable unit economics.
- Regulatory need for data isolation and auditability for certain EU and US customers.

Current stack (what we heard)
- Model hosting: in-house k8s + SageMaker for peak inference.
- Redis for KV cache.
- Mix of CPU and single-GPU endpoints; ops team managing autoscaling.

Success criteria for POC / evaluation
- P95 latency for typical online scoring flows < 150ms (target).
- Predictable monthly TCO within a +/− 15% band vs proposal.
- SOC 2 + audit log capability for requests and model versions.

Decision process and stakeholders (as discussed)
- Technical evaluation: Data Science + SRE (Megan / Ankit).
- Procurement: Procurement team (procurement@finarc.com).
- Legal sign-off: Contracts.
- Expected timeline: technical POC in 3–4 weeks, procurement decision following a successful POC (~6 weeks).

Initial commercial guardrails we suggest for planning
- Target committed monthly spend for a 12-month reserved plan: $30k–$50k (ballpark).
- PoC option: 4–6 week technical evaluation with capped pilot usage; we can offer a limited free credit and lowered reserved starter pricing.

Next steps (proposed)
1) I’ll share a short procurement-outline PDF (attached) with pricing bands and a suggested PoC arrangement.
2) Rishi will follow up with configuration options (quantization, batching, caching) and a rough cost model for your current throughput.
3) Schedule a procurement + legal intro call (suggested window: week of Feb 23). Megan — can you confirm who from procurement/legal should join?

Attachment: redwood-inference-procure-outline-v1.pdf (pricing bands, PoC template, SOC2 evidence links)

Thanks again — I’ll get Rishi to follow up with the configurator output tomorrow.

Best,
Laura
Laura Bennett
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Discovery recap + procurement framing for Finarc analytics evaluation

Thanks, Laura — helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- SOC 2: procurement will need a SOC 2 type II report and a short list of where audit logs are exposed. Do you have a reference pack or a public security page we can share?
- Quantization / quality: our DS team is concerned about any potential quality regression when applying aggressive quantization for latency wins. Can Rishi call out recommended quant profiles and historical evals you’ve run against similar transformer models?
- PoC volume: for the pilot we tend to run a production-representative window (48–72 hours) at peak traffic — that will be the real test for latency spikes.

Procurement contact: I’ll loop them in once we have the pricing bands and SOC2 artifacts (procurement@finarc.com).

I’m available for the procurement intro week of Feb 23; we should include our SRE lead (Ankit) and head of MLops (Priya).

Megan
Megan Liu
Head of Data Products | Finarc Analytics
megan.liu@finarc.com | +1 212-555-0147
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 09:18:00 -0500
Subject: Fwd: Discovery recap + procurement framing for Finarc analytics evaluation

+Laura / Sergio — drafting quick answers to Megan’s questions and proposing internal commercial posture. Notes below (will tidy for procurement doc):

- SOC2 artifacts: we can share our SOC 2 Type II summary and a security packet that highlights audit log endpoints (Console -> Audit -> Exports) and KMS/HSM integrations. I’ll attach the public security page and a short tech note.
- Quantization options: recommend start with 4-bit quantization on candidate models with per-prompt evals for quality; we have historical evals showing <1.5% delta on F1 for reranking and <2% for generation in 80% of workloads. Will include recommended thresholds and fallback to FP16 in critical flows.
- PoC mechanics: propose a 72-hour peak window run in Dedicated sandbox (isolated tenant) with metrics collection: p50/p95/p99, tail latency traces, and token-cost breakdown. We can provide a canonical eval harness to replay representative traffic.

Proposed commercial posture (internal)
- Offer: 6-week technical PoC: 72-hour peak window + 2 weeks analysis. Pilot credits: $8k credit to cover baseline usage.
- Reserved starter band (for planning): 12-month reserved at $0.XX per token / or committed $30k/mo tier with overage rate Y.
- Close blocker: procurement may push for shorter cancellation window; suggest 60-day termination for pilot to align with their legal comfort.

If that looks ok I’ll produce a tidy procurement-outline for Laura to share (includes pricing bands and the PoC template).

-Rishi
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Megan Liu <megan.liu@finarc.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procurement@finarc.com>
Cc: Ankit Sharma <ankit.sharma@finarc.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@finarc.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 10:12:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Discovery recap + procurement framing for Finarc analytics evaluation

Thanks — that all looks reasonable. I’ve shared the procurement outline with procurement@finarc.com and asked them to confirm an available slot week of Feb 23. They requested the SOC2 summary and the PoC template before the call — if you can send those by Monday 2/22 that would be ideal.

For the PoC, we’ll plan the 72-hour peak run and I’ll coordinate the traffic replay with Ankit. Also please include a one-page appendix in the procurement packet that lists the rollback/fallback plan if we observe quality regressions (so our ops team can present to legal).

Talk soon — Megan
